title: Comparing different generations of idealized solar geoengineering simulations in the Geoengineering Model Intercomparison Project (GeoMIP)
abstract: Abstract. Solar geoengineering has been receiving increased attention in recent years as a potential temporary solution to offset global warming. One method of approximating global-scale solar geoengineering in climate models is via solar reduction experiments. Two generations of models in the Geoengineering Model Intercomparison Project (GeoMIP) have now simulated offsetting a quadrupling of the CO2 concentration with solar reduction. This simulation is idealized and designed to elicit large responses in the models. Here, we show that energetics, temperature, and hydrological cycle changes in this experiment are statistically indistinguishable between the two ensembles. Of the variables analyzed here, the only major differences involve highly parameterized and uncertain processes, such as cloud forcing or terrestrial net primary productivity. We conclude that despite numerous structural differences and uncertainties in models over the past two generations of models, including an increase in climate sensitivity in the latest generation of models, the models are consistent in their aggregate climate response to global solar dimming.
problem: It is uncertain whether simulated climate responses to solar geoengineering are consistent across different model generations (CMIP5 vs. CMIP6), given that the newer models have numerous structural differences and increased climate sensitivity, which could alter previously established conclusions.
method: This paper compares climate responses to an idealized solar geoengineering experiment using two multi-model ensembles (CMIP5 and CMIP6) to evaluate whether aggregate climate responses and scientific conclusions are consistent across the two different generations of models.
task: The task is to compare climate model responses from two generations of models (CMIP5 and CMIP6) in an idealized solar geoengineering simulation (GeoMIP experiment G1) where solar reduction offsets a quadrupling of CO2 concentration.
innovation: This paper compares idealized solar geoengineering simulations between two generations of climate models (CMIP5 and CMIP6), finding that aggregate climate responses like temperature and hydrology are statistically indistinguishable, lending confidence to conclusions about the broad climate effects of solar dimming across different model structures.
